cpml.source: Roden and Gedney, Convolution PML (CPML): An efficient FDTD implementation of the CFS-PML for arbitrary media, Microwave and Optical Technology Letters 27(5), 334-339 (2000), https://doi.org/10.1002/1098-2760(20001205)27:5<334::AID-MOP14>3.0.CO;2-A. Compare the same point pulse against a box with twice each dimension.

cavity.source: Balanis, Advanced Engineering Electromagnetics, rectangular PEC cavity TE101: f=c/2 sqrt(a^-2+d^-2).

line.source: Wheeler/Cohn stripline formulas as implemented by Forge rfmath::stripline. A centred strip whose width is much greater than the ground spacing has two parallel-plate TEM channels in parallel. Compare the numerical TEM impedance scaled to w=100 mm, b=1 mm with rfmath's 0.001 mm copper Wheeler approximation; the finite-width and thickness corrections are below 3 percent.

loads.source: Pozar, Microwave Engineering, transmission-line reflection coefficient Gamma=(ZL-Z0)/(ZL+Z0): matched load 0, open +1, short -1.

dipole.source: Balanis, Antenna Theory: Analysis and Design, chapter 4, thin half-wave dipole: shortening to about 0.47 lambda, radiation resistance about 73 ohm, maximum directivity 1.64 (2.15 dBi).

patch.source: Balanis, Antenna Theory, rectangular microstrip transmission-line model, W=c/(2f) sqrt(2/(er+1)), effective er and 0.412h fringing extension. openEMS Simple Patch Antenna tutorial uses the same probe-fed rectangular-patch resonance and broadside pattern: https://docs.openems.de/en/latest/octave/Tutorials/Simple_Patch_Antenna.html; the tutorial describes a nominal 2.4 GHz patch with er=3.38, h=1.524 mm, resonant length 32 mm and width 40 mm, rather than this FR-4 design. The secondary check is against that nominal frequency and broadside behaviour, not a digitized FR-4 trace.

pcb.source: Forge native antenna geometry from MIT tscircuit/core 0.0.2132, 2.4ghz_quarter_wave_monopole, 31 mm radiating arm; free-space quarter-wave estimate c/(4L)=2.417681 GHz, design frequency 2.4 GHz.
